prompt_fields.subject: A regal naga sorceress: humanoid torso rising from a long coiled serpent tail, dark hair falling past bare shoulders, one hand raised holding a barbed trident-spear, the other gripping a carved wooden staff planted against the tail coil. Torso held upright and confident, tail coiled into a stable base rather than sprawled.
prompt_fields.contrast: This is a new humanoid/naga family with no existing catalog member, so no in-family collision; the design goal is a silhouette no other current humanoid or reptile token shares -- the coiled serpent tail base under an upright human torso is the primary cue, reinforced by twin weapons (trident + staff) raised on either side.
prompt_fields.composition: One compact complete creature on a single circular tabletop disc, steep overhead three-quarter camera; visible clear neutral base ring on every side. Keep all anatomy and equipment well inside the inner four-fifths of disc radius. Base brightness must visually match reference neutral disc, with no illumination spill or ground effects. Base-plate discipline, calibrated: prior monster batches measured this exact steep-overhead disc/camera/lighting style rendering on the bright side of the base_drift tolerance by default (batch D's ant redraw averaged +12.2 base_drift on a fresh pass against this same style reference before correction). Render the neutral disc -- including the whole outer-sixth ring band -- about 8 RGB luminance units darker than the style reference's disc appears at first read: a small, deliberate undershoot, not a full shade darker, and not something to eyeball as "looks about right". Do not darken the creature itself to compensate -- only the disc plate takes this small intentional downward bias. Add no warm cast, glow, bounce-light, gradient or vignette to the disc anywhere, including directly under or behind dark-bodied creatures.
prompt_fields.palette: Sun-weathered olive-tan skin, deep violet-black hair, warm gold-red serpent scales fading to pale cream on the coil underside, dull iron trident head, aged driftwood staff; dry neutral charcoal disc with restrained copper-grey bevel, no water pooling on the base.
